name: Bootkit
summary: Adversaries may use bootkits to persist on systems. A bootkit is a malware variant that modifies the boot sectors of a hard drive, allowing malicious code to execute before a computer's operating system has loaded. Bootkits reside at a layer below the operating system and may make it difficult to perform full remediation unless an organization suspects one was used and can act accordingly. strategies.name: Detection Strategy for File Creation or Modification of Boot Files

analytics.name: Analytic 0428
analytics.guidance: Detection of raw access to physical drives, modification of boot records (MBR/VBR), and suspicious file creation or alteration within the EFI System Partition (ESP). Correlates privileged process execution with low-level disk modification and unexpected driver or firmware interactions.

analytics.name: Analytic 0429
analytics.guidance: Detection of suspicious write operations to block devices, modifications of bootloader files (GRUB, initrd, vmlinuz), and unexpected changes within the EFI System Partition. Monitors privileged execution of utilities like dd, grub-install, or efibootmgr that modify boot sectors or loader entries.
